findings.summary: crates/ffi/src/lib.rs:72: the answer time is `self.at(now_ms) + took.elapsed()`, and `took` is a std Instant (CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Android). If the phone sleeps while a read is in flight, the answer is stamped too early and the ages afterwards read older by that sleep. No test covers the term: removing `+ took.elapsed()` passes all of BoardTest and the cargo tests. Taking a second now_ms from Kotlin after the read, or a refresh that returns before finish, would put the whole path on the app's clock.

No cargo test covers the new clock handling. crates/core/tests/reads.rs passes Instant::now() to every Reads::finish call. Making finish ignore its `now` argument (K2), or making Board::at, view or refresh's start use Instant::now() (K1, K3, K4), leaves cargo test -p board-core -p board-ffi green. Only the Kotlin BoardTest.aLongSleepMakesTheBoardOldAndDueAgain catches them, and the Verify gate can't re-run Gradle. A Rust test that finishes at t+8h and checks server_now/refreshed would pin it where the gate can re-run it.

This predates TRU-29 and is outside its scope. The egui native app (crates/app/src/main.rs) still times reads with web_time::Instant, which is std's CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux. After a laptop suspend on Omarchy it would show the same stale '5 s ago' and late refresh that the adversarial review found on Android. It may be worth its own ticket. Under Xvfb with no suspend, the native ages counted up correctly.
